data.description:
# S3 — Bound journald storage and alarm on journal saturation

## Plan
Configure journald with an explicit persistent journal ceiling (`SystemMaxUse` and, if useful, `SystemKeepFree`) using a managed drop-in such as `/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/rebar-disk-ceiling.conf`. Install it through host provisioning/deploy scripts and ensure journald reload/restart behavior is documented and safe.

Extend `infra/scripts/observability.sh` to publish journald usage and cap/percent-of-cap, then add a dedicated CloudWatch alarm for journal saturation. This is separate from the root alarm so operators know the journal is the capped generator consuming its budget.

## Grounding
- The Sep 2 incident measured `/var/log` and journal growth on root; current observability publishes only aggregate root/data disk usage (`infra/scripts/observability.sh:72-90`).
- Compose sends container logs to journald (`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` logging blocks), so journald is an expected accumulator.
- systemd documentation says `SystemMaxUse` controls how much disk persistent journal files under `/var/log/journal` may use, and journald respects the smaller of `SystemMaxUse`/`SystemKeepFree`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Managed journald configuration sets an explicit disk ceiling and is installed idempotently on the Gerrit host.
- [ ] Observability emits a journald usage/cap metric that can be tested without live CloudWatch.
- [ ] Terraform adds a dedicated journald saturation alarm wired to SNS.
- [ ] Runbook documents journal cap, alarm, diagnosis (`journalctl --disk-usage` or equivalent), and safe remediation.
- [ ] Targeted tests cover the generated config, observability metric emission, and alarm wiring.
- [ ] Portability criterion: uses systemd-journald native configuration and local shell/Python tests; no provider-specific CI trigger is required.
